name: accept_issue
description:
Accepts an incoming issue for triage.

Transitions the issue from incoming → accepted.

story_number.description: Optional number of the story to link this issue to

name: assign_issue_to_working_copy
description:
Assigns an issue to a working copy's coding and QA team.

Adds an accepted issue to the team's bag without replacing its current
priority. Assignment clears the team's story assignment and story queue,
even when the issue itself belongs to a story. The first issue establishes
the active priority. Use `set_active_issue`
to prioritize another member and `unassign_issue` to remove one.
Moving an issue preserves its workflow stage and transfers its open tasks.
Coding and QA may work on different eligible issues from the same bag.

Main or the operator can pass `rework: true` and a correction `reason`
for an accepted issue awaiting QA on the same copy. With no open issue
task, this returns the issue to coding and records the instructions;
completed fix tasks remain completed. Ordinary reassignment preserves
the current turn.

reason.description: Why the issue is moving, or the required correction instructions when rework is true

rework.description: Main or the operator requests corrections to a submitted fix on the same copy. Requires a reason and no open issue task; preserves completed task history.

working_copy_id.description: Working copy whose coding and QA team takes the issue

name: create_issue
description:
Record an issue against the project (`scope: app`) or against
CodeMySpec itself (`scope: framework`).

If you encounter undocumented config, a looping hook, a tool error,
or contradictory prompts inside CodeMySpec, your FIRST call is
`create_issue` with `scope: framework` — before asking the human
operator and before working around the problem. The framework is
the system you are operating inside; friction with it is a
first-class issue, not a question to escalate or a workaround to
invent.

Trigger examples (use `scope: framework`):

- Confusing or contradictory prompts/instructions
- Looping stop hooks or stuck workflows
- Tool or MCP server malfunctions (not an external source returning HTTP 404)
- Missing, broken, or poorly documented tools
- Suggestions for improvements to the system

For project-side bugs and feature gaps (the app under development,
not CodeMySpec), use `scope: app` (the default).

Severity must be critical, high, medium, low, or info. `error` and `warning`
are analyzer finding levels, not issue severities.

Issues land as `incoming` and are triaged by the human operator. Be
specific in your description — include the exact error message, what
you were doing, and what you expected to happen.

description.description: Detailed description of the issue including steps to reproduce if applicable

scope.description: Issue scope: app (default), qa, docs, or framework

session_id.description: Injected by hook — do not set manually

severity.description: Issue severity: critical, high, medium, low, or info

source_path.description: File path where the issue was found, if applicable

story_number.description: Number of the related story, if applicable

name: dismiss_issue
description:
Dismisses an incoming issue with a reason.

Transitions the issue from incoming → dismissed.
Requires a reason explaining why the issue was dismissed.

name: get_issue
description:
Gets a single issue by ID with full details.

Accepts a full id or a unique prefix — the 8-character form every commit
message, comment and issue body in this codebase uses.

Use list_issues to find issue IDs.

issue_id.description: Issue ID, full or a unique prefix (use list_issues to find IDs)

name: list_issues
description:
Lists issues in the caller's active project with optional filters.

Defaults to open issues (incoming and accepted), across all scopes and
severities. Results retain the default limit of 50 and disclose truncation.
In scripts, the result contains `issues`, `matched`, `returned`, `limit`,
`truncated`, `project_total`, `filtered_out`, and `filters`; iterate
`result.issues` to read the rows.

Filter by status (incoming, accepted, dismissed, resolved),
severity (critical, high, medium, low, info), scope (app, qa, docs,
framework), or story_number.

`framework` used to be excluded here, on the grounds that framework issues
routed to the hosted server rather than being stored locally. That stopped
being true when the tools moved onto the server — see `CreateIssue`, which
writes every scope the same way — so they were creatable, visible in an
unfiltered listing, and impossible to filter for.

limit.description: Most issues to return, newest first (default 50)

query.description: Text that the title or description contains (case-insensitive)

scope.description: Filter by scope: app, qa, docs, framework

severity.description: All severities by default; all, or one of critical, high, medium, low, info

status.description: open (default: incoming and accepted), all, or one of incoming, accepted, dismissed, resolved

story_number.description: Filter by the related story's number

working_copy_id.description: Filter by assigned working copy; all severities are included unless filtered

name: resolve_issue
description:
Resolves an accepted issue with a resolution description.

Transitions the issue from accepted → resolved.
Requires a resolution explaining how the issue was fixed.

name: set_active_issue
description: Prioritize an accepted issue already assigned to a working copy. This changes the team priority without removing other issues from its bag.

name: submit_story_issue
description: Submit a story-owned fix with the exact revision and validation evidence.

issue_id.description: Issue belonging to your assigned story

revision.description: Exact committed revision containing the fix

name: unassign_issue
description: Remove an issue from its working copy bag. Open tasks must be dispositioned first. Other assigned issues remain available.

name: unassign_issue_from_working_copy
description: Remove an issue from its working copy without resolving it.

name: update_issue
description:
Update non-status fields on an existing issue.

Use this for re-triage decisions that don't change the issue's
status — most commonly severity adjustments after a closer look
at the body, or moving an issue under the right story / category
after the original report misclassified it.

Status transitions (incoming → accepted / dismissed, accepted →
resolved) go through the dedicated `accept_issue` / `dismiss_issue`
/ `resolve_issue` tools — those flows enforce transition rules
this tool deliberately skips.

Allowed fields: `severity`, `story_number`, `category`, `source_path`,
and `append`.

## Why `append` and not `description`

An agent files an issue at the moment it has the evidence, which is
often before it understands the defect — and that is the right time
to file, because the evidence is perishable. So reports go stale,
and until now the only remedy was another issue: `1f60a145` cited
`server.log` for a stop hook that posts to :4004 and logs to
`web.log`, which sent its reader to a process that was not involved
and a log showing no activity. Correcting it took a second issue,
`b0486568`, and the queue then held two reports of one defect with
the first still misleading whoever picked it up.

This appends rather than replacing, because issue bodies are written
by whichever agent was there and a later reader needs to see what
was originally claimed as well as what turned out to be true. A
correction that quietly rewrites the first account destroys the one
thing that makes the sequence legible.

Status transitions still go through `accept_issue` / `dismiss_issue`
/ `resolve_issue`.

append.description: Add a correction or later evidence to the end of the issue body. The original text is kept — use this instead of filing a second issue to correct a first.

detach_from_story.description: Detach the issue from whatever story it is on, leaving it unattributed. For a report that reached the wrong story — `Issues.attribute_to_story/3` sweeps unattributed :app issues onto whichever story's QA attempt is being submitted, so an infrastructure failure can end up gating a feature story. Sometimes the right story is none.

severity.description: New severity: critical, high, medium, low, or info

story_number.description: Re-link the issue to the story with this number
